definition: DBRX is a large language model (LLM) developed by Mosaic under its parent company Databricks, released on March 27, 2024 under the Databricks Open Model License.
details: It is a mixture-of-experts transformer model, with 132 billion parameters in total. 36 billion parameters (4 out of 16 experts) are active for each token. The released model comes in either a base foundation model version or an instruction-tuned variant. At the time of its release, DBRX outperformed prominent models such as Meta's Llama 2, Mistral AI's Mixtral, and xAI's Grok-1, in several benchmarks ranging from language understanding, programming ability and mathematics. It was trained for 2.5 months and reported using on 3,072 Nvidia H100s connected by 3.2 terabytes per second bandwidth (InfiniBand), for a training cost of US$10M.

explainer.lead: DBRX is a large language model from Mosaic and Databricks that uses a mixture-of-experts design to keep only part of its 132 billion parameters active for each token. Released on March 27, 2024, it showed how this approach could deliver strong benchmark results while activating 36 billion parameters at a time.

tiers.eli5: DBRX is a computer program that works with language, a bit like a team of 16 specialists. For each small piece of text, it calls on four specialists instead of making the whole team work. It comes in a general version and another version trained to follow instructions.
tiers.practitioner: Choose between the base foundation model and the instruction-tuned variant according to whether you need a general model or one prepared for instructions. Distinguish the 132 billion total parameters from the 36 billion active per token when planning capacity, and review the Databricks Open Model License before use.
tiers.paperLevel: DBRX is a mixture-of-experts transformer with N_total = 132 billion parameters, E = 16 experts, k = 4 active experts per token, and N_active = 36 billion parameters. Training took 2.5 months on 3,072 Nvidia H100 GPUs connected by 3.2 TB/s InfiniBand bandwidth, at a reported cost of US$10 million. Release-time comparisons reported advantages over Llama 2, Mixtral, and Grok-1 on several language, programming, and mathematics benchmarks, without establishing results beyond those comparisons.

explainer.example: If the instruction-tuned model receives a request to solve a mathematics problem, its expert-routing machinery selects four of the 16 experts for each token. Those experts contribute to processing that token while the other 12 remain inactive.

flow: A token enters the transformer model.
The mixture-of-experts machinery selects four of the 16 experts for that token.
The selected experts process the token using 36 billion active parameters.
The model continues transformer processing to produce its output.
explainer.origin: Mosaic developed DBRX under its parent company Databricks and released it on March 27, 2024 under the Databricks Open Model License. Its training lasted 2.5 months and had a reported cost of US$10 million.
explainer.lineage: At release, DBRX was reported to outperform Meta's Llama 2, Mistral AI's Mixtral, and xAI's Grok-1 in several benchmarks covering language understanding, programming, and mathematics.
explainer.whyItMatters: DBRX demonstrates a large mixture-of-experts language model in which only a fraction of the total parameters is used for each token. Its release also provided both base and instruction-tuned variants under the Databricks Open Model License.
